finding.claim: The DELETE /projects/:id handler calls authorized(), which returns a boolean, and ignores the result. Any authenticated user can delete any project, including projects they do not own. The sibling PUT handler calls authorize(), which throws on failure, so this looks like a mix-up between two near-identical function names.
finding.source: Any authenticated user sends DELETE /projects/<id> with an arbitrary project id (req.params.id).
finding.sink: req.store.projects.delete(project.id) at api.js:19, a destructive operation on another user's project.

trace.note: project is loaded by attacker-supplied id with no ownership filter
authorized(req.user, project) returns false for a non-owner, but the return value is discarded and nothing throws
authorized() only returns a boolean and never throws, unlike authorize() at api.js:4

finding.guards_checked: authorize() at api.js:4 throws on failure but is not used in this handler. authorized() at api.js:12 is called without checking its result. I found no middleware or other check in the file, and the file is the whole repository. The only unseen control would be auth middleware that sets req.user, which cannot enforce ownership.

verdict.guard_found: authorize() at api.js:4 throws 403 but is only used in the PUT handler (api.js:25). authorized() at api.js:12 returns a boolean, and its result is discarded at api.js:18. No middleware or other check exists, and api.js is the only file.
verdict.reason: At api.js:18 the boolean from authorized() (defined at api.js:12-14, which never throws) is discarded, so api.js:19 deletes the project for any authenticated non-owner, unlike the PUT handler that uses the throwing authorize() at api.js:25.
